search_method: Bounded format-specific comparison of four named C++ XML parser libraries; exact Debian binary-package and Homebrew formula lookups, all hits recorded in registry-snapshot.json
ranking_metric: Debian popcon installations of the library's -dev package(s) (by_inst)
selection: Xerces-C++ and pugixml rank first and second on Debian dev-package installs: libxerces-c-dev 2,676, libpugixml-dev 1,503, then libtinyxml2-dev 487 and libxml++ dev packages 275 (266 + 7 + 2). Both are built and control-verified; they are distinct parser families (Apache Xerces-C++ scanner vs pugixml's own single-file parser).
uncertainty: Pilot cell: Xerces-C++ 3.3.0 and pugixml 1.16 were built and control-verified. Homebrew install-on-request (365d) orders the four differently: tinyxml2 1,757, pugixml 1,270, Xerces-C++ 1,209, libxml++ 461, so the order depends on the metric; Debian dev installs remain the one primary metric. Source-level popcon is not used because libxml++2.6's 79,794 count is a runtime pulled in by dependents (79,361 with no recent file access). tinyxml2 and libxml++ stay unresolved leads in leads.json. libxml++ parses through the libxml2 C library. Whole frameworks (Qt, Boost, POCO) were not ranked. The ISO C++ standard library has no XML API. pugixml does no namespace processing: its namespace-resolved output comes from adapter code over pugixml's qualified names, so namespace well-formedness is checked by the adapter, not the library. pugixml also skips DOCTYPE without expanding DTD entities. Two small UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity declaration, validation, non-UTF-8 encoding or XML 1.1 behaviour; attributes are reported sorted per element because DOM NamedNodeMap order is unspecified.
